newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa reverses, ends weaker after NY fall.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa reverses, ends weaker after NY fall.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended weaker in cross-dominated dealings on Monday as traders took profits on a widening arbitrage after speculative sales in New York.

Prices were hovering near their lows but with the market generally stuck in a vicious downtrend, the shorts, which are believed to outnumber the longs, were reluctant to cover their positions just yet, traders said.
"The market is not in a hurry to rally back up. There are still residual bits of cocoa around," said one.
West African crops were still coming down the pipeline, although in the last few days origins seemed to be reluctant to sell at current prices.
The benchmark May contract ended the day seven stg lower at 867 stg a tonne after touching a high of 879 stg in early trading. It went down to 865, avoiding a further slip to its life-low of 855 stg.
Much of the day's 18,720 lots turnover was concentrated on crosses between March and December initiated by Phibro, traders said.
Some 6,000 lots were crossed on each side of the deal, apparently to roll March shorts forward before the first notice day next week. The contract expires at the end of March.
"The open interest in March should be interesting. It will come down tomorrow," said the trader.
Cocoa prices sagged in New York as the market ignored the weakness of the dollar and London's earlier efforts to rise, widening the arbitrage against London.
Prices rose at the outset, but with no follow-through quickly reversed in a speculative bout of selling. The CSCE May contract traded down to $1,258 a tonne but was off it low at $1,268 at 1730 GMT.
Traders were awaiting an update on arrivals data from the Ivory Coast to gauge supply levels later this year.
"The only interesting thing is what the arrivals are in Ivory Coast," said one. "It's so crucial," said one trader, adding that weekly arrivals were expected to taper off in the coming weeks.
Attentions are now focused on the development of the Ivorian midcrop and the effect of hot and dry weather conditions on the trees.
